paragraphs.text: Octopuses are widely regarded as the most intelligent invertebrates. In laboratory studies, they have learned to open screw-top jars, navigate mazes and recognise individual human keepers. Unusually, about two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located not in its brain but in its arms, which can respond to touch and taste independently. Despite these abilities, most octopus species live for only one to two years, which means that they have little opportunity to learn from others; their intelligence appears to be largely individual rather than social.
